finding.text: `ai/AISession/AISessionConversation.js` is a second chat renderer. `ext/Chat/Chat.js` already does exactly this job: its `chat({ source, keep })` returns `.view` and `.sync()`, it draws each line once (a `seen` set), has smart scroll, labels each sender, and has `place_card` for inline cards. The brief (law 6: "look before writing one") asks to reuse the existing component, so feed the transcript entries into `ext/Chat` and drop the new class, or say in the doc why it cannot be used.

Step 1 says "stream, never poll", but `AISessionFollow.js:12` only shortens the `setInterval` + `fetch` poll from 3000 to 1000 ms. That is still polling and about 10x slower than the ~100 ms asked for. `doc/realtime.md` describes a dev-socket push (`session_index`), and `ext/JSONL` has `live()`. Use one of those, or add a per-line socket feed. If that has to wait, write it down as an open item in the doc instead of calling the page live.

Step 5 is not met. Cards are read once at load (`AISessionDetail.load_cards`), they sit in the side column instead of inline at their time, and nothing shows that a card the mastermind posts appears live. `doc/session-cards.md` admits this under "Not yet". Nothing confirms that `page_add`/`page_note` actually write `{"card":{title,text,href}}` lines, so the chosen format may never be produced by any tool. Check what the tool writes, then show one real card arriving live, inline (`ext/Chat`'s `place_card` may already cover the inline part).

The first `pull()` passes the whole transcript to `on_lines`, so `AISessionConversation.add` draws every message of a long session and only then trims to 200 (`AISessionConversation.js:43-44`). Slice to the newest 200 messages before drawing.

The "stay at the bottom" check uses `document.scrollingElement` (`AISessionConversation.js:42`). The page is `width: "fill"` inside a panel, and if the panel scrolls rather than the document, the check is always wrong. Moving to `ext/Chat` (finding 1) fixes this too.
The `load_transcript` call is gone from the `Promise.all`, but the static `AISessionDetail.load_transcript` (around line 148) is now dead code. Delete it, or leave a comment saying who still uses it.
The "No transcript" message only shows on the follow path. A non-uuid id that falls to `load_lines` and gets nothing shows an empty column.

There are no screenshots at 1400 and 3440 in the review folder, so I could not verify steps 3 and 4 ("conversation within ~200 px", "fills the width"). The `cols main-aside` layout looks right in code.

None of the screenshots show the session page. The six shot folders are old task pages (2026-10-02 page-extends-item, task-audit, 2026-10-03 data-grid, prompts-live, push-to-talk, sessions-tab-polish). They were picked only because the diff appended `{"gone":true}` lines to their `page.jsonl`. So asks 3 and 4 (the conversation starts within ~200 px at 1400; the body fills the width; checked at 1400 and 3440) have no proof. The work is also not on michael/dev yet: `AISessionConversation.js` is missing from the main tree, so a live shot can't stand in.

The "N tool calls" lines land in the wrong place. In `AISessionConversation.add` these entries have no `at`, and `ext/Chat`'s `sync` sorts each batch by `Date.parse(a.at ?? 0)`, which puts them before every message. On the first load, every tool-call line would pile up at the top of the history instead of sitting between turns (ask 2).

A reply that also calls tools has its tool calls counted twice. `run += m.tools` runs before `flush()`, so the reply's tools go into the line drawn above it, and then `run = m.tools` counts them again in the line below it (ask 2).

Ask 1 said "stream, never poll", but `AISessionFollow.EVERY_MS` went from 3000 to 250: a range-request poll every 250 ms. The reason is stated in code and in `doc/session-cards.md` (the transcript lives outside the repo, so the dev socket can't watch it). It is still a poll, and the per-line server push remains open.

Cards may not show "at their time" (ask 5). `add_card` uses `c.ts` from the item, falling back to now, and each card is synced in its own batch, so it is drawn after whatever is already on screen, not at its place in the timeline. If the cards stream arrives before the first transcript pull, cards are drawn above the whole history.

The diff carries about 45 unrelated `files.jsonl`/`page.jsonl` "gone" lines across old task folders, plus `ai/files.jsonl` marking `CLAUDE.md`, `usage.json` and `tasks.json` as gone. That is watcher noise. It misled the shot picker (finding 1) and should not land with this task.

`ext/Chat/Chat.js` and `Chat.css` were edited outside the fence (a `recent` window plus a "show earlier" button). Reusing the one chat component is right under law 6. The change touches every chat surface, though, and no chat surface was shot.
`this.cards` is assigned after several awaits. If the page is deactivated first, the `Cards` stream is never unsubscribed.
